blockers.title: After 'Elimina il corso', the erased course's students come back: a refusal of a queued upload is recorded after the erase, listed under the next course, and 'Riprova l’invio' restores the erased course and student and queues them again
blockers.evidence: The erase empties uploadRefusals, but the queue still holds the earlier transaction with full student rows; refused after the erase, they are written back into uploadRefusals with their personal data. At a627810 retryUploadRefusals re-inserts them unchecked; in the working tree, with the erase's deletes held up, the course refusal passes parentsPresent (courses has no parent check), then the student passes too. Observed: 'refusals after erase+refuse: 2 PUT:courses:other-account,PUT:students:access'; 'student first names kept after erase: ["Ottavia"]'; after Riprova 'device after retry: {"courses":2,"oldBack":true,"active":2,"students":["Ottavia"]}'.
blockers.reproduction: Scratch Playwright specs (fake backend of tests/e2e/b4-uploads.spec.ts): backend unreachable, create D2 with synthetic 'Ottavia Sintetico', sign in and let the switch queue; erase the course; the backend comes back refusing the old inserts with 403/42501 (deletes still failing in the working-tree variant); create a new course and open Impostazioni: the alert counts the old rows, uploadRefusals holds the student, Riprova restores the erased course.

importantFindings.title: An edit or delete of a row in another account's course is not refused: the server answers 204 with zero rows, so at a627810 it counts as uploaded
importantFindings.evidence: Live, two test accounts, synthetic course (cleaned up): account 1 PATCHing account 2's course or student: 204, 0 rows; DELETE: 204, 0 rows; upsert: 403/42501. At a627810 uploadEntries does not read back the affected rows. The working tree adds select and serverHasRow; whether that lists such a PATCH as a refusal was not checked.

importantFindings.title: Deletes of minors' data lose to device clocks: a conditioned delete and keep_latest_edit let a later updatedAt keep a deleted student or course on the server
importantFindings.evidence: DELETE ... WHERE updatedAt <= previous updatedAt, and keep_latest_edit skipping older updates, compare device-set times; a deletion on a phone whose clock is behind another phone's last edit is skipped, counted only as superseded, and the data comes back on sync. The erase's course delete is conditioned the same way. Follows owner decision 12, but no rule says a delete of personal data should lose.
importantFindings.reproduction: By construction (the trigger is not yet on the development backend).

qolFindings.title: The minimum writer is a compatibility gate, not an access control: x-cvc-app-version is client-asserted
qolFindings.evidence: Any client can send 999.0.0; acceptable since RLS bounds every write. Setup sound: search_path '', EXECUTE revoked, RLS on app_minimum_writer with no policy; live: app_minimum_writer 404 PGRST205, rpc 404 PGRST202. A future server-side writer through the Data API (B6) must send the header. The migration should say it is not a security boundary.

qolFindings.title: A version over int range raises 22003, classified as 'data' instead of 'outdated'
qolFindings.evidence: string_to_array(sent,'.')::int[]; only a malformed client can send it.

qolFindings.title: After a network failure, uploads did not retry for 20 s while the sync stream was also unreachable, until the app reopened
qolFindings.evidence: Scratch log: 't 0..3 pending 4 refusals 0 writes []' over 20 s with the fake backend back; writes went out after the reload.
